test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following provisions is provided in the cylinder head during design for increasing the air cooling effect?

options.text: Dimple like shapes on surfaces are provided on the cylinder walls.
Cylinder head is provided with water jackets.
Cylinder block is provided with high speed cooling air flow.
Fins or extended surfaces are provided on the cylinder walls and cylinder blocks.

solution:
The correct answer is __Fins or extended surfaces are provided on the cylinder walls and cylinder blocks**(Option 4)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fins or extended surfaces__ are used to enhance the cooling effect in air-cooled engines.
 
• The fins increase the surface area of the cylinder head and cylinder block, allowing better heat dissipation into the surrounding air.
 
• This design is commonly used in small engines such as motorcycles, scooters, and lawnmowers.
 
• The fins are specially shaped to ensure maximum heat transfer efficiency.
 
• Airflow over the fins is generated either by vehicle motion or by a dedicated fan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Water Jackets:**

 
 
• They are used in water-cooled engines to circulate coolant and remove heat.
 
• This is a different method of cooling compared to fins.
 
 
 
• **Dimpled Surfaces:**
 
 
• Dimple-like shapes are not typically used for cooling cylinder walls but are sometimes applied in other engineering contexts to reduce drag or increase turbulence.
 
 
 
• **High-Speed Cooling Airflow:**
 
 
• Although air motion aids cooling, the primary cooling effect in air-cooled engines comes from fins, not just airflow.
